One pathway involves Mebhydrolin, a decongestant, while the other involves Dexchlorpheniramine, an antihistamine. Both Mebhydrolin and Dexchlorpheniramine are indicated for Vasomotor Rhinitis, indicating that Desonide may be indirectly associated with this condition through these medications. The final scores, though not directly measuring the strength of the Desonide-Vasomotor Rhinitis relationship, suggest a moderate level of support for this connection through the indicated chain of medications. The evidence is consistent across two paths, but the strength of the relationship is somewhat weaker in the second path, likely due to lower scores. The mechanism appears to involve the use of medications that target different pathways of Vasomotor Rhinitis, suggesting a possible indirect therapeutic relationship.
